analysis:
Both changed files are documentation only (docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md and docs/developer/build.md). No code, config or endpoint changes are present.

prefix-cache.md changes:
- Table row at line 295 now lists the plain unpublished Nemotron Super owner as eligible for the opt-in resident recurrent checkpoint bank.
- Lines 300-306 add `alignsRecurrentCheckpointsToPrefillChunks`. Nemotron Super checkpoints are captured only at multiples of its fixed prefill chunk reached by whole chunks (`NemotronSuperLocalPrefixCache`).

Security relevance:
- The change is described as resident-only, behind `DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY=1` and the global switch (line 287).
- It is tenant-scoped by `cacheSalt` (line 331-332).
- Per the doc's "Only the recurrent bank currently publishes resident-ready routing evidence" section, it needs verified identities. It writes no state to disk (line 340).
- This is consistent with T-041 and SEC-035, whose at-rest posture is unchanged: SSD stays HMAC-keyed with a 30-minute TTL.
- The resident bank does widen the in-process same-account TTFT oracle surface (T-041/SEC-035) to another model, but only on explicit opt-in. I do not treat that as a regression.

build.md adds a section about portable Nemotron qualification fixture harnesses (`scripts/nemotron-qualification/README.md`). It explicitly disclaims qualifying the shipping provider. The 88-shard checksum verifier has no visible change here.

No security controls change. Unverified: whether the code behind the new doc claims (Nemotron Super owner, chunk alignment) exists or behaves as described. That is outside the supplied evidence, so I record it as a coverage limit rather than a finding.
